milestone: M4: the workout application — logging, timers, substitutions and offline-first persistence, on the iPhone and laid out for desktop. 61 small PRs in 15 tracks, revised against origin/main 8c0a31b, M3's plan with its pushed m3/14 and m3/15, M2's onboarding plan and the M2X brief (desktop view and email sign-in link). Two of them are fallbacks, built only if M3 declines the logging amendments this plan delivers to it now. It starts with two slices that can merge now: an SVG sprite that takes 1.8 KB off every route (M2's, M3's and M2X's next route nodes wait for it), and the hooks' security headers for prerendered pages through vercel.json. Next come a pure wire contract (the offline workout sync ADR) with one shared kit fixture, the logging rules for every measure and load type, superset flow, and one projection function that is the reconciliation rule. Then the on-device store, outbox and sync engine: every request bounded, a change that keeps failing surfaced to the owner, and what the server holds deleted when the session is lost. Two serial migrations follow M3's last slot (a sync ledger, then pain reports), then the exactly-once sync API, run segments and session records edited by piece, and the reads. Each workout kind is its own prerendered, offline-capable route with its own budget runway: strength at /workout, runs at /workout/run, other sessions at /workout/session. The strength screens are built against the shared kit fixture in IndexedDB, so that track never waits for the server chain, one capability per PR, each designed and tested at the iPhone viewport and at 1440 × 900. Every refused change has a Fix or a Discard, by mutation type. Nothing links to the workout until the whole loop works and sign-out protects unsynced sets (dark launch). Parallel tracks cover runs and sessions, plates, in-workout actions including the owner's own exercises, History beside its detail on desktop, and the entry points. A perf gate runs from the first logging slice. Three journeys, the owner's screenshot review and the final measurements (INP p75 over five loads) follow, and one docs slice closes the milestone.

ONE CONTRACT: WIRE FORMAT v1 (workout-contract).
- The envelope is {v, id, type, workoutId, entityId, at, payload}.
- 16 mutation types:
  - workout.start, workout.update, workout.finish, workout.abandon
  - set.log, set.skip, set.edit, set.delete
  - exercise.skip, exercise.substitute, exercise.dislike, exercise.create
  - pain.report
  - run.log, run.segment
  - other.log
- Device-only actions are never sent: the current exercise, drafts, an added exercise, attached server data (kit.attach), the rest timer and the stopwatch.
- Identity rule:
  - A create's id is its new row's client id: workouts.client_id, set_records.client_mutation_id, or the substitution's, segment's, pain report's or custom exercise's id. So id === entityId.
  - Edits, deletes, finish and abandon get a fresh crypto.randomUUID and address rows by client id, never by a server id. An edit made offline before its create synced therefore still works.
  - A run segment's first run.segment creates it (id === entityId); every later one edits it, with a fresh id and the same entityId.
  - A workout has at most one run record and one other-session record, and its own id is workout.start's. So run.log and other.log always carry a fresh id, with entityId = the workout: the first one creates the record, every later one edits it with absolute values.
- Entity keys: workout:, set:, segment:, run:<workout>, other:<workout>, slot:<workout>:<position> and exercise:<id>. A mutation that names a custom exercise still in the outbox depends on its exercise.create.
- The wire format is M4's own. The server maps it onto M3's services, so a late M3 rename changes one adapter, not the client.
- After merge, only optional fields and new types are added. v changes only together with a server that accepts both versions.

THE DEVICE STORES INPUTS, NOT DERIVED STATE, AND ONE FUNCTION IS THE RECONCILIATION RULE (the offline workout sync ADR).
- For each workout, IndexedDB holds the start kit, the server's canonical rows (keyed by client ids, tombstones included) and the device state. The outbox holds the pending mutations.
- Every screen shows project(table, kit, canonical, pending in outbox order, device state), with the route's reducer table (decision 5). That one pure function serves:
  - the optimistic UI (one mutation through the same reducer, in the same frame)
  - restore
  - other tabs and other devices
  - every sync response
- Reducers are idempotent by entity: a create of an existing id is a no-op (tombstones included), edits are absolute, and deletes leave tombstones. Replaying a mutation the server already applied therefore changes nothing.
- Conflicts:
  - The server applies mutations in arrival order: the last applied wins, and M3's training_audit records both.
  - A device's own pending edit wins locally until it is acknowledged.
  - A pending edit of a set deleted on another device is parked as 'Deleted on another device', for Discard.
  - The server never overwrites device state.
- A seeded convergence property holds: project(kit, serverModel(M[0..k]), M[i..n]) for any i ≤ k+1 equals the fold of M. It runs in the domain, and again against Postgres through the real endpoint, reordering only across rows, because the outbox keeps each row's mutations in order and same-row edits end with the last applied by design.

LOGGING RULES FOR EVERY MEASURE, LOAD TYPE, SUBSTITUTE AND SUPERSET live in pure domain modules, so the logger, the prefill, the summary, the schemas and the server agree.
- Measures (logging-rules): a reps set records reps, a time set seconds, a distance set metres.
- Load types:
  - external: a completed set needs a weight
  - bodyweight: an optional added weight; blank means bodyweight only
  - assisted: the assistance, stored in its own column (A1); lower is harder
  - none: no load field at all
- Counting:
  - e1RM only for external-load reps sets, on top of M3's setE1rm rules
  - volume load: weight × reps on external loads, added weight × reps on weighted bodyweight sets, nothing on assisted, unloaded, time and distance sets, which report reps, seconds and metres totals instead
  - PRs: e1RM and rep maxes on external loads, and 'most reps' on unweighted bodyweight sets. No PRs on assisted sets in M4.
- Substitutes (set-prefill):
  - A substitute never inherits the original's absolute, percent_1rm or from_e1rm load. As in M3's swap, such a load becomes rpe_based at the same RPE.
  - Its weight comes from the substitute's own last top set, which the kit's alternatives carry, or from its own previous sets once attached; otherwise it is left blank with the RPE instruction.
  - Its own load type decides the field, so pull-up → assisted pull-up asks for assistance.
- Supersets (workout-flow):
  - consecutive exercises with the same superset number alternate A1 → A2 → A1, with no rest inside a round and the round's rest after its last member
  - a member with more sets continues as straight sets
  - a skipped set advances like a logged one
  - manual navigation never breaks the alternation that follows, because the next step is computed from logged counts
  - Up next names the partner, and the screens label members A1, A2, B1…

EXACTLY ONCE: A LEDGER ON TOP OF M3'S REPLAY CONTRACT.
- M3 makes creates idempotent by client id, edits absolute and deletes soft. Two gaps remain:
  - finish, abandon, and a dislike with its program swap create no unique row
  - an old edit replayed after a newer one from another device would overwrite it
- sync_mutations records every applied id in the same transaction as its effect (INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING). A concurrent duplicate waits on the uncommitted key, then reads 'seen'.
- Each mutation runs in its own transaction. Results:
  - applied
  - duplicate: canonical rows returned, nothing applied
  - rejected: dotted field errors
  - deferred: its target has not arrived
  - retry: a transient failure, which stops the batch
- Rejected, deferred and retried mutations leave no ledger row, so Fix re-sends the corrected payload under the same id, in its place (planner A). Fix may even change the type: a refused dislike can be re-sent as today's substitution.
- Within a batch, once one of a row's mutations is refused or deferred, that row's later mutations are deferred too.
- Batches are capped at 25 mutations and 64 KB; the pagehide keepalive batch at 48 KB.
- Rejected:
  - one endpoint per mutation (round trips for an offline backlog)
  - last-writer-wins on client clocks (clock skew)
  - per-row version locking (it refuses the owner's own offline edits)
  - Background Sync (not on iOS)

ONE INDEXEDDB DATABASE: 'pc-offline', the name M2's sign-out already deletes.
- It goes through idb 8 (about 1 KB), with every store declared at version 1: workouts, outbox, kits, library, meta.
- dispatch applies a mutation and its follow-up local actions (a superset's next set, a created exercise's substitution) in memory, then writes them in one readwrite transaction: the outbox entries and the device state together.
- Transactions await nothing but IndexedDB, because Safari commits a transaction that awaits anything else.
- Quota and private-mode errors surface as 'Not saved on this device', on the action that failed, with Retry.
- BroadcastChannel 'pc-workout' tells other tabs: changed, purged, closed or signed-out.
- The Web Lock 'pc-workout-sync' keeps one flusher per device (Safari 15.4+). Without it, the ledger deduplicates.
- The connection closes on versionchange, and the store refuses to write again until the page reloads. Sign-out's deleteDatabase is therefore never blocked, and a stale tab can never recreate the data.
- Other screens read through a raw-IndexedDB probe that never creates the database.
- A 'pc-offline' with other stores (M2's sign-out specs create one with a single 'sets' store, fact 23) reads as empty to the probe, to sign-out's pending check and to the sign-in page, and the workout store deletes and recreates it when it opens it.
- storage.persist() is requested when a workout starts.
- idb and fake-indexeddb are M4's only new packages, and they land in one slice.
- Logic lives in plain .ts, because the unit project excludes *.svelte.test.ts. Thin .svelte.ts wrappers use $state.raw over the reducer's immutable objects, never $state.snapshot, and no binding is named after a rune (fact 5).
- The store's read path is in the workout pages' initial JS, because it is the data path. This departs from docs/performance.md's M4 sketch, and the departure is documented. The sync engine loads on idle.

FLUSHING.
- Order: strict FIFO by outbox sequence, with entity-key dependencies. A parked or waiting entry blocks only its dependants.
- Backoff: full jitter, random × min(60 s, 1 s × 2^attempt), reset on success and on 'online'.
- Bounds: a sync POST is aborted after 15 s and a reconcile GET after 10 s, on the engine's own timer (an AbortController, never AbortSignal.timeout, so tests control it). An abort counts as a failure, backs off and releases the Web Lock, so a hung request on 'lie-fi' never holds the flusher.
- Surfacing: counted failures are a 'retry' or 'deferred' answer for the entry, or a 5xx or timeout of a batch it heads; an offline device counts nothing. After 50 counted failures, or 24 hours since the first, the entry is parked as 'Needs attention' with its last error, Try again (which clears the count) and Discard. Nothing retries in silence for ever.
- A 404 on reconcile: while the workout's workout.start is pending, keep everything and reconcile after the flush. After the start was acknowledged (the server lost it, as after a restore), keep the local copy and every pending change; their sends answer deferred, so the cap above surfaces them.
- One engine per page. The shared Shell starts it on idle and subscribes it to the store's onChange (workout-sync-wiring), so a dispatch from any view or sheet triggers a flush. So do 'online', becoming visible, app start and the backoff timer.
- On pagehide, a keepalive send capped at 48 KB, so RUM's sendBeacon still fits in the page's 64 KB keepalive quota.
- Session loss and sign-out follow the next decision. Nothing unsynced is discarded unless the owner chooses Fix or Discard.
- While changes are pending, the resume bar loads the engine on any (app) screen, so a workout finished offline syncs wherever the owner goes next.

LOSING THE SESSION NEVER LEAVES PERSONAL DATA BEHIND, AND NEVER DROPS UNSYNCED SETS SILENTLY.
- 401 (the session was signed out elsewhere, revoked from Security, or expired):
  - The engine deletes everything the server already holds: saved kits, canonical rows, the cached library, and synced and finished workouts. It keeps only the unsynced outbox entries and the device-only state of an unfinished workout.
  - The workout pages then show 'Signed out on this device · N changes waiting — Sign in to continue', with no workout details.
  - After sign-in the outbox flushes, and the view is rebuilt from the server (adoptRemote, with the kit re-fetched by its pinned session).
  - A device that stays offline keeps showing its workout until it next reaches the server. Signing out on the device itself clears everything.
  - This goes into the ADR and into docs/security.md's threat model.
- 403 passkey_required (a recovery session): 'Finish adding your passkey to sync', keeping everything. Any other 403: backoff, never a purge.
- Sign-out from the app (signout-workout-data) flushes first (≤ 5 s), asks before deleting what remains, clears the device, then leaves a one-shot marker for the sign-in page.
- The sign-in page's ?signedOut=1 clear runs in full only when that marker is present. Without it (a no-JavaScript sign-out, a stale link, another tab), it keeps unsynced outbox entries, deletes everything else, and says 'This device still holds N workout changes that haven't synced'. It offers Sign in to sync them, and Delete them (with confirmation).

NO SLOT TABLE (planner B over planner A's workout_exercises). The server's canonical workout is complete without one. It is made of:

- its pinned planned session, whose immutable rows give the planned slots
- sets carrying the exercise id, position and planned lineage

- pain_reports
- the run and other-session records
Skipping or stopping an exercise writes skipped set rows. An exercise added mid-workout is device state until its first set syncs; this is documented. SUBSTITUTION AND PAIN SEMANTICS live in one pure table and copy module (substitution-rules) and in the server handlers (substitution-handlers, pain-handler).
- Machine unavailable writes only M3's workout_substitutions row (equipment_unavailable): never a preference, never a program version, as asserted in SQL. Alternatives that need none of the slot's equipment rank first, and each alternative shows what it needs.
- I don't like this asks for explicit confirmation, then sends one exercise.dislike mutation. In one transaction, behind one ledger row, it runs:
  - M3's recordExercisePreference (source 'workout', under the per-owner lock)
  - M3's never-again swap from today, when the slot still holds the exercise in the current version. It re-bases onto whatever version is current under the program lock (A6's base 'current'), so a dislike made offline against an older version never meets ADR 0010's compare-and-set as a conflict. When the slot is gone from the current version (swapped or skipped on Train since), only the preference and today's substitution are recorded; the preference keeps the exercise out of every generated week. No conflict is ever parked for the owner.
  - today's substitution (reason dislike)
- This hurts writes a pain_reports row, never a preference. 'Stop this exercise' comes first, then the kit's gentler options for the chosen area, then 'End the workout here' when it is severe, which opens the finish summary. The copy links to Profile → Injuries for a lasting problem.

- The area rules are server-side data (domain/programming/pain.ts), built on M3's avoidance rules, so what an area excludes has one definition.

slices.title: feat(workouts): apply workout mutations exactly once, in order, through POST /api/workouts/sync
slices.goal:

1. Claim its id in the ledger. 'seen' means duplicate: nothing is applied again, and the canonical rows come back.
2. Validate it: the schema, then the exercise's load type with logging-rules' checkSet.
